SMTO-SKL-0052 — Google Drive didn't send back a usable answer

GUID: d5d2a40a-0ac1-5f7f-8b9e-808cce6424e5
Slug: google-drive-provider-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO asked Google Drive for information, but Google didn't answer, the connection dropped, or the answer was garbled. This happens while reading, so nothing in your Drive was changed by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to the internet, for example by opening drive.google.com in a browser on it. SMTO already tried up to three times, so a dropped or blocked connection is the most common cause.
  2. Wait a few minutes, then ask SMTO for the same Google Drive information again. Google Drive sometimes has short outages; this step only reads, so asking again is safe.
  3. If you had also asked SMTO to change a file in the same request, open Google Drive and check whether that change already happened before asking for it again. A change that was cut off may still have gone through, and repeating it could do it twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists or shows the Google Drive files you asked for without this error.

If it still fails

  • If drive.google.com works in your browser but SMTO still fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't share your Google password or sign-in links.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned a server-side failure, the connection failed after automatic read retries, or the response had a malformed file, list or page-token shape.

What this means

  • Drive encounters server/transport failures or rejects malformed collection, cursor or file identity data. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Drive encounters server/transport failures or rejects malformed collection, cursor or file identity data.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish endpoint failure from response-validation failure using recorded safe details.

How to fix it

  • Check network reachability from the Server to www.googleapis.com and Google Workspace status; DriveClient.request already retried the read up to twice (transport errors, 5xx and short Retry-After rate limits). If the response was malformed (validate_file, DriveService._page, or a mismatched file id in _info), capture the Server log for the call and retry the read later; inspect any separate uncertain write before repeating it.
  • Inspect the recorded status or invalid response, restore a usable read, and reconcile uncertain writes before repetition.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry reads later; inspect any uncertain write before another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized bounded read returns coherent same-resource data.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
